tutorial.title: Using Flex Direction
tutorial.descriptionContent: Learn how to quickly rearrange HTML elements with Flexbox.

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent: Flexbox helps us build a game HUD layout (like hearts, score, and items) without changing the HTML. Press the buttons to see it in action.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
To control the direction HUD elements are displayed in, we use the flex-direction property.

Make sure to pick flex-direction.

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
The default value for flex-direction is row. Flexbox HUD elements have this value even if we don't code it.

Make sure to pick row.

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
flex-direction: row means HUD slots start from the left of the container and are shown horizontally in the order they're in the HTML.

Make sure to pick row.

lessons.title: Lesson #5
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can also set flex-direction to column. Here, the HUD slots begin at the top and are placed vertically in the order they're in the HTML.

Make sure to pick column.

lessons.title: Lesson #6
lessons.interactiveContent:
When flex-direction is set to column, HUD slots stretch out to fill the container's width.

Make sure to pick column.

lessons.title: Lesson #7
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does this code display?

Flex items aligned in a columnFlex items aligned in a row

Flex items aligned in a column.

lessons.title: Lesson #8
lessons.interactiveContent:
What is the default flex-direction value applied to a game HUD flex container?

rowcolumn

Make sure to pick row.

lessons.title: Lesson #9
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does flex-direction: row do?

It displays elements horizontally from left to rightIt displays elements horizontally from right to left

It displays elements horizontally from left to right.

lessons.title: Lesson #10
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does flex-direction: column; do?

It displays elements vertically from top to bottomIt displays elements horizontally from top to bottom

It displays elements vertically from top to bottom.

lessons.title: Lesson #11
lessons.interactiveContent:
How do we know these HUD slots will be 200px wide?

Because flex-direction: column; means they stretch to fill their container's widthBecause that's how wide the body element is

Because flex-direction: column; means they stretch to fill their container's width.

lessons.title: Lesson #12
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code the flex-direction property.

Make sure to type flex-direction.

lessons.title: Lesson #13
lessons.interactiveContent:
Set flex-direction to its default value.

Make sure to pick row.

lessons.title: Lesson #14
lessons.interactiveContent:
Make these HUD messages display in a single row.

Make sure to type row.

lessons.title: Lesson #15
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code column to make the HUD messages display in a column.

Make sure to type column.

lessons.title: Lesson #16
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code the margin so that the HUD slots can stretch to 200px in width.

Make sure to pick 0px.

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent: In game UI, you may want HUD elements to start on the opposite side, like mirroring a score bar. Flexbox can flip the layout direction.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
To change the starting position of HUD items to the right side of a bar, we can use row-reverse.

Make sure to pick row-reverse.

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
flex-direction: row-reverse means HUD items start from the right of the bar and are shown in the order they're in the HTML.

Make sure to pick row-reverse.

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
If we want to reverse the direction of a vertical HUD list, we can use column-reverse.

Make sure to pick column-reverse.

lessons.title: Lesson #5
lessons.interactiveContent:
flex-direction: column-reverse means items start from the bottom of the panel and are shown in the order they're in the HTML.

Make sure to pick column, followed by -, and finally reverse.

lessons.title: Lesson #6
lessons.interactiveContent:
With column-reverse, the flip is easier to notice when the panel is taller than the items.

Make sure to pick 300px.

lessons.title: Lesson #7
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does row-reverse do?

Reverses the starting position for HUD items displayed in a rowMakes HUD elements display in a column

Reverses the starting position for HUD items displayed in a row.

lessons.title: Lesson #8
lessons.interactiveContent:
What will this code display?

The labels GOLD, XP, MP, HP on the right side of the barThe labels HP, MP, XP, GOLD on the right side of the bar

The labels GOLD, XP, MP, HP on the right side of the bar.

lessons.title: Lesson #9
lessons.interactiveContent:
What will this code display?

The labels Map, Key, Bomb, Potion in a columnThe labels Potion, Bomb, Key, Map in a row

The labels Map, Key, Bomb, Potion in a column.

lessons.title: Lesson #10
lessons.interactiveContent:
What happens when we set flex-direction to column-reverse;?

HUD items start from the bottomHUD items start from the top

HUD items start from the bottom.

lessons.title: Lesson #11
lessons.interactiveContent:
What happens when we code flex-direction: column-reverse; without setting a height value for the panel?

The panel's height is the total height of its itemsThe panel's height is the same as the <body> element's height

The panel's height is the total height of its items.

lessons.title: Lesson #12
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code row-reverse.

Make sure to type row-reverse.

lessons.title: Lesson #13
lessons.interactiveContent:
Set the flex-direction property to the appropriate value to make Score appear near the right edge of the HUD bar.

Make sure to pick row-reverse.

lessons.title: Lesson #14
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code column-reverse.

Make sure to pick column, followed by -, and finally reverse.

lessons.title: Lesson #15
lessons.interactiveContent:
Make P1 appear near the bottom edge of the panel when flex-direction is set to column-reverse.

Make sure to pick P1, followed by P2.

lessons.title: Lesson #16
lessons.interactiveContent:
Starting from the bottom of the panel, display Boss, Wave, and Level in that order. Keep in mind the flex-direction is column-reverse.

Make sure to pick Boss, followed by Wave, and finally Level.
